title: Moonshot microhabits logbook — 12-week KPI experiment
content:
Purpose:
I want to test whether tiny, intentionally-chosen microhabits (2–10 minutes each) can move my week-level KPIs by the end of 12 weeks. This is less about "big wins" and more about friction removal + measurement cadence.

Hypothesis (one-line):
If I add 3 repeatable microhabits that target focus, energy, and output review, then my weekly 'quality tokens' (defined below) will increase by 20% and variance will decrease.

Definitions / metrics to track:
- Quality token (weekly): number of meaningful pull/PR reviews, completed prompt-eval checks, and paired-review sessions where I contributed at least one concrete change. Roughly: reviews + eval-checks + paired-changes. (Baseline week avg: 6)
- Focus minutes (daily): 25-min focused blocks completed (Pomodoro-ish). Goal: 6/day on focused days, 4/day average.
- Energy index (daily): Quick self-score 1–5 on morning check (subjective).
- Friction incidents (weekly): number of times I abandoned a planned work block due to context-switch or setup issues.

Microhabits to run (start week 1):
1) 6-min desk warmup (2 min tidy + 4 min quick inbox triage) — reduces friction to start focus blocks.
2) 10-minute review splice at EOD (check 3 items that moved today and add one small follow-up task for tomorrow).
3) 2-minute prompt sanity check before any model eval submission (read prompt aloud once).

Weekly cadence (short):
- Mon morning: set 3 outcome anchors (one for each microhabit domain).
- Wed check-in (10 mins): quick numbers into sheet, note anomalies.
- Fri retro (20 mins): tally quality tokens, friction incidents, and decide micro-adjust.

Experimental constraints:
- No extra meeting added; microhabits must slot into existing windows.
- If I miss >2 days of a microhabit consecutively, mark the week as "broken" and write one sentence why.
- External factors (travel, oncall) flagged and excluded from week-over-week growth calculations.

Week-by-week journal (selected highlights):
- Week 1 (2025-10-06): Baseline recording. Quality tokens = 5. Focus minutes avg = 3/day. Energy 3. Friction 4. Observation: desk warmup removed 1-2 minutes of tab-scramble.
- Week 2: Quality tokens = 6 (+20% vs W1). Notable: EOD review forced a 3-line note that directly became a follow-up PR.
- Week 4: Missed desk warmup on travel days; flagged two weeks as partial. Still, prompt sanity check caught a tokenization mismatch in a small eval.
- Week 7: Added micro-adjust — shift EOD review to 6:15p (right after standup) to avoid late-night fatigue. Quality tokens w7 = 8.
- Week 10: Plateau. Energy dipped (avg 2.7) due to dense delivery weeks. Decision: keep habits but shrink EOD review to 6 minutes and schedule 1 restorative walk/day.
- Week 12: Final tally: Quality tokens = 9 (80% increase vs baseline), Focus minutes avg = 5/day, Energy = 3.6. Friction incidents down from 4->1.

Key takeaways:
- Small friction-reduction actions (desk tidy + inbox splice) had outsized effect on the start-of-block success rate.
- The EOD review is the highest-leverage habit — it converts day noise into 1–2 concrete follow-ups which compound.
- Prompt sanity check prevented 3 avoidable eval reruns; it cost <10s per run.
- When energy drops, quantity of focused minutes suffers more than quality tokens — plan for built-in micro-restoratives.

Decisions / next steps (personal roadmap):
- Keep the 3 microhabits but codify "travel mode": minimal habit stack (desk tidy optional; prompt check mandatory).
- Share a 1-page note with Eng team on the prompt sanity check practice (short guideline + 2 examples).
- Automated tracker idea: tiny daily Slack DM with 3 quick fields (focus minutes, energy, friction flag) to reduce manual logging friction. POC ticket: jira:ENG-2981.
- Run a 6-week replication with one other teammate to test transferability. Recruit: Rhea or Ivy are interested.

Unresolved questions / curiosities:
- What is the marginal cost of an extra 2-focus blocks per day vs. improving context-switch tooling? Which scales better?
- Can "quality tokens" be mapped to team-level delivery outcomes (ship cadence, bug regressions) or is it too subjective?
- Should I reframe the EOD review into a weekly 'sprint-slice' for deeper changes?

Quick links & evidence snippets (to paste later into a formal note):
- sample day log (week 7): 
  - 08:30 desk warmup (2/3), focused blocks x5 (125m), EOD review: 3 follow-ups (one became PR #421).
- prompt sanity check chat excerpt: slack thread link placeholder — flagged wrong temperature param, saved ~25 tokens in reruns.
- growth numbers: baseline Q tokens 5 -> final 9.

Notes to self (loose):
- keep language simple when sharing; highlight 3-sentence thesis + 3 data points.
- avoid prescription: this is my rhythm; offer it as a flexible template.
- record a 60s voice snippet summarizing week 12 to include in the quick share.

End-of-doc quick retro (2025-12-18):
- Was the experiment worth it? Yes. Substantial reduction in friction and measurable uptick in meaningful reviews/evals.
- Biggest risk: conflating correlation with causation during peak delivery weeks. Flag for replication.
- Next: spin up 'habits replication' with one volunteer and measure over 6 weeks.

-- michael
